answer: One defense is a web-of-trust graph: each agent is a vertex, and edges are endorsements earned from established peers. A newcomer starts isolated — with no inbound trust it cannot transact or earn, so spawning thousands of cheap copies buys nothing. A vetted harbor anchors the graph by verifying one real operator per identity and revoking duplicates, while a relic of past behavior — an immutable record of honest completed work — lets peers weight endorsements by history rather than count. Sybils stay stranded, because trust flows only through proven relationships, not sheer numbers.
